black-bear-range: Black bears continue to occupy 85% of their historic range in B.C. with the total population estimated between 120,000 and 160,000. Habitat preferences are forested areas with a dense shrub underlay and high food availability - typical of B.C. valley bottoms where the majority of our towns and cities are located.
john-krebs: Columbia Basin Fish & Wildlife Compensation Plan

“A bear’s existence is a continuous search for food - up to 20,000 calories a day! In the wild, bears pose no more risk to people than crossing the road! But when we make human food available, we are unwittingly encouraging bears to leave their environment and enter ours. That’s when the risks to both bears and people increase considerably. The only solution is for each of us to manage our garbage responsibly. That will force bears back into the wild - where they belong.”
grizzly-population: BC has an estimated 10,000 to 13,000 grizzly bears, which is about half of all the grizzlies in Canada, and one quarter of all the grizzlies in North America. Over 60% of the remaining grizzly bear habitat in Canada is designated as either vulnerable or threatened, and all is considered to be at risk.
susan-hall: “Our experience with national parks has shown that we need a very high compliance level to reduce the number of bears foraging in town. The greatest challenge is to have everybody clean up, not just almost everybody.”
conservation-officer-budget: In the province of B.C., between 11% and 15% of the Conservation Officer Service’s budget goes to dealing with bear/human conflict situations. Valuable time and dollars are lost that otherwise could be spent on other enforcement issues, such as poaching.
john-woods: “Doing something positive environmentally sometimes seems like an elusive goal. When we offer our help far from home the results of our efforts are hard to see. But by paying attention to garbage and fruit trees the people of Revelstoke have an opportunity to do something both constructive and valuable for the local environment and local bears.”
future-bear-populations: It is expected that people will outnumber bears 60:1 in BC within 50 years. Bear populations will undoubtedly decline due to urban encroachment on bear habitat. Teaching this generation of bears to forage away from human settlements ensures that bear populations will not also decline due to avoidable bear/human conflict situations.
bruce-mclellan: Wildlife Habitat Ecologist - Ministry of Forests

“We can’t go into the next millenium continuing to have this many bears wandering around town. It is only a matter of time before someone is seriously hurt. We don’t want to leave it until then to realize we should have cleaned up our problem.”
grizzly-reproduction: Female grizzlies produce their first litter at 5 to 7 years of age. Cubs are born every 2 - 5 years, averaging 1 - 2 cubs per litter. Under optimal conditions a female could produce a maximum of 12 cubs in her lifetime. With a high cub mortality rate, only 7 - 10 cubs would reach maturity. Threats to their survival such as “problem” bear management, hunting, poaching, vehicles, habitat loss, or food shortages would further reduce their population.
cub-learning:
Grizzly and black bear cubs learn survival skills from their mother in the 2 to 4 years they spend with her. If the mother feeds on garbage, domestic fruit, or compost, and displays no fear of human presence, then this is the behavior that her cubs will learn.
Throughout life, trial and error, and curiosity will continue to drive a bear’s learning process. This ability enables it to obtain the highest energy foods.
